name: Lee Kang-sheng
bio: Lee Kang-Sheng  (Chinese: 李康生; Pinyin: Lǐ Kāngshēng; b. 1968 in Taipei, Taiwan) is a Taiwanese actor, film director, and screenwriter. He has appeared in all of Tsai Ming-liang's theatrical feature films. Lee's own directorial efforts include The Missing (2003) and Help Me Eros (2007).

credits.overview: On a seesaw, Sun and Moon rise and fall, witnessing four feasts and festivities spanning four millennia, where the living and the dead, gods and ghosts unite in a simple, shared joy.

credits.title: Stray Dogs
credits.overview: An alcoholic man and his two young children barely survive in Taipei. They cross paths with a lonely grocery clerk who might help them make a better life.

credits.title: Letters from the South
credits.overview: Six filmmakers present six short films about the experiences of Chinese immigrants. Shot across Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore and Myanmar, the anthology depicts the crisis of identity that accompanies international migration.

credits.overview: A contemplative trip down memory lane with one of the leading voices of the Second New Wave of Taiwanese Cinema. Saw Tiong Guan clearly established a very personal bond with his subject, and also found many of Tsai Ming-liang’s colleagues prepared to complete this portrait of a quiet yet outspoken artist.

credits.title: Sleepwalk
credits.overview: A continuation of Tsai Ming-Liang's Walker series, featuring Lee Kang-Sheng as a barefoot monk who walks very slowly.

credits.title: No Form

credits.title: Beautiful 2012
credits.overview: A collection of shorts by four East Asian directors: Ann Hui on a male-to-female sex change, Kim Tae-yong on an emotional imposture, Gu Changwei on pregnancy in China and Tsai Ming-Liang on time and the city of Hong Kong.

credits.title: Transformation
credits.overview: In order to recreate a photograph, two actors undergo a transformation.

credits.overview: Taipei 24H divides 24 hours in Taipei into 8 shorts. credits.title: Visage
credits.overview: Hsiao-Kang, a Taiwanese film director, travels to the Louvre in Paris, France, to shoot a film that explores the Salomé myth.

credits.title: Remembrance
credits.overview: About remembrance, of course, but also about the aromas that remain after farewell. A woman says farewell to her coffee shop after 20 years. A regular client is the only person to share this special moment with her. On the radio, farewell to a beloved dancer. With Tsai Ming-liang as the regular client.

credits.title: Sleeping on Dark Waters
credits.overview: A behind-the-scenes documentary on the making of Ming-liang Tsai’s I Don’t Want to Sleep Alone.

credits.title: To Each His Own Cinema
credits.overview: Commissioned to mark the 60th anniversary of the Cannes Film Festival, "To Each His Own Cinema" brought together 33 of the world's pre-eminent filmmakers to produce short pieces exploring the multifarious facets of cinema and their perspective on the state of their chosen artform in the early 21st century.

credits.title: Help Me, Eros
credits.overview: Having lost all his money in the stock market, a depressed man falls in love with a woman over a suicide helpline.

credits.title: It's a Dream
credits.overview: Shot in an abandoned cinema in Malaysia, Tsai Ming-Liang's home country, It's a Dream evokes the filmmaker’s earliest encounters with cinema and recalls the golden age of Asian film culture.  An extended version of the filmmaker's short created for the Canne Film Festival's "To Each His Own Cinema".

credits.title: I Don't Want to Sleep Alone
credits.overview: A Bangladeshi immigrant living in harsh conditions nurses an injured man back to health, but when the recovering man falls for a waitress, their tender bond is tested by competing affections.

credits.title: The Wayward Cloud
credits.overview: Hsiao-Kang, now working as an adult movie actor, meets Shiang-chyi once again. Meanwhile, the city of Taipei faces a water shortage that makes the sales of watermelons skyrocket.

credits.title: My Stinking Kid
credits.overview: Drama about a young boy who suffers from a rare deficiency disease. The medicine he has to take every day has the side effect of making him reek of ammonia. credits.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
credits.overview: On a dark, wet night in Taipei City, a cavernous old picture palace is about to close its doors forever. A meager audience, the remaining few staff, and perhaps even a ghost or two, watch King Hu’s wuxia classic "Dragon Inn", each haunted by memories and desires evoked by cinema itself.

credits.title: The Missing
credits.overview: A grandmother is looking for her grandson, a teenager for his grandfather.

credits.title: The Skywalk Is Gone
credits.overview: A young woman wandering around meets a young man going to a casting call for a pornographic film.

credits.title: Looking for Tsai
credits.overview: Human shortcomings in the pursuit of an idol. Two film school students travel to interview Taiwanese film director Tsai Ming-liang and actor Lee Kang-sheng in Oslo.

credits.title: A Way We Go
credits.overview: For the past forty years, Ah Long has headed up a traditional Chinese musical troupe. But times are changing, and the troupe members leaving one by one, Ah Hui, is an aimless slacker with no plans for the future. Ah Hui’s best friend is Ah Gou, a young man who works as a welder making metal gates.

credits.title: What Time Is It There?
credits.overview: A street vendor with a grim home-life forges a connection with a young woman on her way to Paris.

credits.title: The Moon is Gone
credits.overview: There are 365 moons in the sky, with one falling every day to meet with the world. However, on the Mid-Autumn Festival, the moon begins to feel it is not appreciated by the people of the world. Feeling deserted and sad, it then gets eaten by a dog.

credits.title: Sunny Doll
credits.overview: Hsin-He, a high school sophomore who can get along just fine on her own, lives with her father. At school, the days pass slowly by, until one day, she is assigned to be the student teacher. Since she loaths math, her teacher orders Ke-Lei, student teacher from another class, to tutor her.

credits.title: Ordinary Heroes
credits.overview: Ordinary Heroes narrates the life stories of an advocate, a prostitute, a social worker, and a priest during Hong Kong’s social movements of the 1970s and 1980s. The film is based on true events.

credits.title: The Hole
credits.overview: In the final days of the year 1999, almost everyone in Taiwan has died from a strange plague that ravished the island. As rain pours down relentlessly, a single man is stuck with an unfinished plumbing job and a hole in his floor. This results in a very odd relationship with the woman who lives below him.

credits.title: The River
credits.overview: A young man develops severe neck pain after swimming in a polluted river for a movie shoot, but nobody can provide him any relief.

credits.title: Sweet Degeneration
credits.overview: With a singular voice that distinguishes him from his New Taiwan Cinema contemporaries, Lin Cheng-sheng adds to his brief, but already remarkable, filmography with Sweet Degeneration, his third film in two years. credits.title: A Drifting Life
credits.overview: After his wife dies during childbirth, Ku-cheng leaves his children behind in their rural village while he finds work on a construction site in the city. He develops a relationship with a widow but despite their intimacy, he refuses to remarry.

credits.title: My New Friends
credits.overview: Tsai interrupted his pre-production for The River to make this pioneering documentary for Taiwan's nascent AIDS-awareness campaign. credits.title: Vive L'Amour
credits.overview: Three lonely young denizens of Taipei unknowingly share an apartment: May, a real estate agent who uses it for her sexual affairs; Ah-jung, her current lover; and Hsiao-kang, who's stolen the key and uses the apartment as a retreat.

credits.title: Rebels of the Neon God
credits.overview: In Taipei, four youths face alienation, loneliness, and moments of existential crisis amidst a series of minor crimes.

credits.title: Boys
credits.overview: A junior-high student bullies and blackmails a younger boy, then receives the same treatment at the hands of some older students.
